_about: Invite message library. The server picks one line from each of the four parts, fills the placeholders, and never reuses a combination already sent. 20 x 20 x 20 x 20 = 160,000 unique messages. Members cannot type or edit a message, but Shuffle draws a fresh combination.

placeholders.{guest}: Guest's first name, exactly as the inviter typed it
placeholders.{inviter}: Inviter's first name (the admin uses their own first name too)
placeholders.{key}: The guest's access key, e.g. VELVET 4827

notes: {covered} is a space plus one line from covered_lines, only when the inviter has already paid for this guest. Otherwise it is empty.
{key_line} is one line from key_lines, chosen at random.
The link must sit on its own line so WhatsApp builds the preview card from it.
Store the four indexes used (e.g. [3, 11, 0, 17]) on the invite, with a unique constraint, so a combination is never sent twice.
Shuffle draws a new unused combination. The previous one is released back to the pool if it was never sent.

rules: Never mention the date, venue, price, dress code or other guests. Messages get forwarded and screenshotted.
The invite part (everything above the link) stays under 60 words, plus the covered line when it is used. The longest possible combination today is 59 words with long names, 70 with the covered line.
No dashes between clauses. Keep the house voice: warm, calm, a little mysterious, never salesy, never shouty, no emojis.
